title: Root dethronement via version bump attack
description:
## Location
rust/lichen-rpl/src/dodag.rs lines 331-354, 399-409

## Issue
A malicious node can dethrone a DODAG root by sending a DIO with a higher version number. The root will call `adopt_version()` which transitions its role from Root to Unjoined and clears its state, allowing the attacker to become its "parent".

## Attack sequence
1. Root is at version 0, rank 256
2. Attacker sends DIO with version=1, rank=256 (valid parent params)
3. `version_is_newer(1, 0)` returns true
4. `candidate_admissible()` passes (uses INFINITE_RANK for node/lowest rank during version check)
5. `adopt_version(1)` is called unconditionally
6. Root role transitions to Unjoined (allowed by state machine)
7. Root clears parent table, sets rank to INFINITE
8. Attacker DIO is accepted as parent candidate
9. `select_parent()` runs, root joins under attacker

## RFC 6550 violation
The DODAG root IS the version authority. Non-root nodes must not be able to force a version change on the root. RPL expects authenticated DIOs to prevent spoofing, but even with authentication, any joined node could claim a higher version.

## Suggested fix
Add early return in `process_dio()` for root nodes:
```rust
if self.role == DodagRole::Root {
    return DioOutcome::Rejected;
}
```
Or: reject newer-version DIOs when role is Root, since roots define versions.
close_reason: Fixed: Root nodes now early-return DioOutcome::Rejected in process_dio() before any version/parent processing can occur. The SECURITY comment at lines 324-327 documents the attack vector this prevents.
